> Adaptive High-Speed Stable Line-Following Robot The Adaptive High-Speed Stable Line-Following Robot is an autonomous vehicle designed to follow a predefined path while achieving a balance between  high speed, accuracy, and stability. Unlike conventional line-following robots that move at a fixed speed, our robot continuously analyzes the position of the line using an IR sensor array and adjusts its motor speed and direction accordingly. When the robot detects a straight or gentle section of the track, it automatically increases its speed to reduce the overall travel time. When it approaches a sharp curve or detects a larger deviation from the line, it reduces its speed and applies stronger steering correction to maintain stability and prevent the robot from leaving the track. The main focus of the project is to minimize lap time while reducing unnecessary left-right oscillations. The robot will be tested at different speeds and on different track sections to determine the maximum speed at which it can maintain reliable and stable line tracking. The project demonstrates how sensor feedback, motor speed control, and adaptive algorithms can be combined to improve the performance of a low-cost autonomous vehicle using basic components.
